sources.construction_method: 1975 publication indexing USGS flood-prone area maps prepared through July 1974, listing quadrangle, actual flood year/design frequency, index reliability
sources.quality_basis: Original March 1975 USGS WRI 74-48 index, compiled 1975-01-16; RECON=no detailed surveys/H&H; STANDARD=surveys and detailed H&H; HIGH=surveys/H&H plus observed flood evidence. This is retrospective map quality, not an accurate numerical RMSE or proof the 1975 map existed in 1937.

sources.quality_basis: Site-specific gage datum, observation date, old gage record and unit; remarks record March 1913 and Jan 31 1937, not NAVD88.

sources.quality_basis: Regional flood episode timeline only; flood stage gage and actual county influence must be separately established.

limitations: Current NFHL geometry is not a verified historical map snapshot.
NFIP claims/policies are administrative context, cannot be joined to individual buildings, addresses, or parcels from public redacted data.
USGS model-based inundation maps are not FEMA BFE determinations and do not by themselves prove maps used during an event.
Modern 2012–2026 LiDAR and building footprints are post-event for 1937, often for 2011; preserve acquisition vintage.
No 1937 parcel-level BFE or regulatory NFIP panel can have existed; FEMA/NFIP was established decades later.
No source tile checksum, digital map edition or asset geometry is attached to this inventory.

USGS 1975 index records cover historical inundation maps prepared after 1937; index HIGH/RECON is a qualitative reliability class, not numeric surveyed accuracy or proof of actual agency map use in 1937.
The March 1975 USGS index includes 1937 observed-event inundation maps and 100-YR design maps, which must not be conflated. The original images themselves and GIS polygons have NOT been retrieved.
